title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
author: Juan Antonio Vega Coso
description:
arXiv:2610.16454v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
author: Xingxing Xu, Minjia Shi, Jon-Lark Kim
description:
arXiv:2610.16121v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
author: Jakob Cimprič
description:
arXiv:2610.15887v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellensätze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

title: Low-rank perturbation of symplectic matrices
author: Christian Mehl
description:
arXiv:2610.20646v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
author: Jakob Cimprič
description:
arXiv:2610.15869v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellensätze for free modules.

title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
author: Chengming Bai, Vladimir Dotsenko, Guilai Liu, Hongjie Wang
description:
arXiv:2610.15858v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
author: Hideto Asashiba, Ayako Itaba, Manuel Saorin
description:
arXiv:2610.15517v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We consider a family $(Λ_λ)_{λ\in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $λ\in \Bbbk^\times$, $Λ_λ$ is socle equivalent to $Λ_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $Λ_λ$ is not derived equivalent to $Λ_1$ if $λ\neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
author: Andrea Sciandra
description:
arXiv:2610.15473v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
author: Niels Lauritzen, Jesper Funch Thomsen
description:
arXiv:2610.15469v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

title: Cohen-Macaulay truncated path and Nakayama algebras
author: Takahiro Honma, Satoshi Usui
description:
arXiv:2610.15386v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: This paper characterizes Cohen-Macaulay algebras in the sense of Auslander and Reiten [Progr. Math. 95(1991)] within the following two classes of finite dimensional algebras: (i) truncated path algebras and (ii) Nakayama algebras. For the former, our characterization in terms of ordinary quivers shows that if a Cohen-Macaulay truncated path algebra $Λ$ is connected, then $Λ$ or $D(Λ)$ gives a dualizing module, where $D$ denotes the standard duality. For the latter, we show that every Cohen-Macaulay Nakayama algebra $Λ$ is Iwanaga-Gorenstein. In particular, $Λ$ always gives a dualizing module. Consequently, there is no non-trivial Cohen-Macaulay algebra among truncated path and Nakayama algebras.

title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
author: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru
description:
arXiv:2610.15347v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous. On the other hand, the categorical approach leads naturally to new classes of Yang-Baxter solutions. Our approach consists in identifying suitable subcategories of the category $\mathcal{YB}$ of Yang-Baxter solutions and providing categorical characterisations of the solutions they encode. As an application, we prove that the category of Płonka bi-magmas is isomorphic to the subcategory of $\mathcal{YB}$ consisting of solutions of the Baaj-Long-Skandalis equation. Along the way, we introduce and study a new class of Lyubashenko type solutions and examine the extent to which non-degenerate bijective solutions of the braid equation arise from skew left braces.

title: Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories
author: Mikhail Dusman, Alexander Pavlov
description:
arXiv:2610.14931v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction. We also introduce quasiprojective pairs of adjoint functors and prove a coherence criterion that generalises the criterion of Gomez Pardo and Martinez Hernandez to arbitrary Grothendieck categories. Finally, we extend Stenstr{ö}m's characterisation of coherence via FP-injective modules to compactly assembled Grothendieck categories: such a category is coherently assembled if and only if the class of CM-injective objects, defined through compact morphisms, is closed under filtered colimits. Along the way we revisit the various equivalent conditions for the coherence of a ring, collecting them in a single place. The proofs make use of the compactly assembled categories of Efimov.

author: Alexander Frolov
description:

Abstract: Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $σ(t^q)=t^{2q}$. title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $σ$-Complete Embedding
author: Joaquim Reizi Higuchi
description:
arXiv:2610.14859v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $σ$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $π_aπ_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.

title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
author: JiaJia Han, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.14838v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.

title: The $E_6$ normal forms: semisimple deformations, geometry, DT invariants, and the $E_{6,\infty}$ order
author: Shengyong Pan
description:
arXiv:2610.13745v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study the completed Jacobi algebras of $x^3+xy^3+p(y)$ for $\operatorname{ord}_yp=n\ge4$. The explicit normal-form morsification, the filtered length and centre proofs, and the cyclic terminal identities give finite free semisimple deformations. For every parameter of finite order we construct a polynomial curve neighbourhood and a local projective small contraction; the resulting geometric GV and Donaldson--Thomas calculations identify the block multiplicities. The one-dimensional limit $E_{6,\infty}$ is studied separately as an order: we determine its normalization, conductor, radical-idealizer chain, and maximal overorders. The canonical chain yields a nine-dimensional finite quotient whose Ringel dual is isomorphic to its opposite. An expanded construction gives a choice-independent $22$-dimensional quotient and a $40$-dimensional Ringel dual; a corner quotient relates the two finite constructions. The length and centre formulas are proved by a filtered comparison with a homogeneous matrix order and by terminal identities at the exceptional endpoint.

title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
author: Vladimir G. Tkachev
description:
arXiv:2610.13532v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary. These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.

title: Projective Differential Moment Invariants from the Viewpoint of Classical Invariant Theory
author: Leonid Bedratyuk
description:
arXiv:2610.13229v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Polynomial first-order projective differential moment invariants are investigated. The main result establishes an exact correspondence between such moment invariants and symmetric polynomial multipoint relative projective differential invariants of weight $-1$. This correspondence describes each homogeneous component with respect to moment degree and allows previously obtained results on relative projective invariants to be used for systematic construction. It is also proved that passing from the formal algebra of moments to their integral definitions introduces no additional algebraic relations among the constructed invariants. For low moment degrees, the absence of nontrivial invariants of degrees $1$ and $2$ is established, and a complete description of degree $3$ invariants is obtained. The ten cubic differential moments are naturally identified with the coefficients of a ternary cubic, connecting the construction with classical invariant theory. In particular, the Aronhold invariants $S$ and $T$ yield projective differential moment invariants of degrees $4$ and $6$. One of the known moment invariants of Wang et al. is shown to be proportional to $S$. The algebra of polynomial moment invariants is proved not to be finitely generated. The field of rational moment invariants coincides with the field of fractions of the polynomial invariant algebra. For the explicit constructions, compact multipoint representations define the corresponding moment polynomials without requiring their full expansions. These representations provide a basis for algorithmic construction and software computation of the invariants.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
author: Pavel Chebotarev
description:
arXiv:2610.14100v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$, and we describe $Λ_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$. For a vector whose components are the $n$ distinct $n$th roots of unity, every $Z_i(v)$ equals $S_n$. We then show that the conjecture is false for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with one vertex duplicated has an eigenvalue lying $2.1\cdot10^{-4}$ beyond one edge of $S_7$. For the analogous digraph of order $n$, the corresponding eigenvalue lies at signed distance $δ_n\sim\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$ beyond the supporting line of the analogous edge of $S_n$, so the construction yields counterexamples for all sufficiently large $n$; numerically, it does so for every $7\le n\le300$. We also prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$, with $S_m\setminus\{0,1\}$ lying in the interior of $S_n$ for $n\ge3m$.

title: Global obstruction property and its applications
author: Weiheng Xia
description:
arXiv:2610.12583v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite. For each Artin algebra $A$, we construct an algebra $\mathcal{G}(A)$ satisfying GOP by using triangular matrix extensions. We show that $\text{fin.dim}\mathcal{G}(A)=\text{fin.dim} A+2$ and that $A$ and $\mathcal{G}(A)$ are singularly equivalent. Finally, we give a pair of derived equivalent finite-dimensional algebras for which GOP holds on only one side.

title: Sharp commutator bounds on complex simple Lie algebras: the Böttcher--Wenzel inequality and the comass of the Cartan $3$-form
author: Daniel J. F. Fox
description:
arXiv:2610.11800v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For a complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ with compact conjugation $τ$, Killing form $B$, and Hermitian form $H(x, y) = -B(x, τy)$, it is shown that $H([x,y],[x,y]) \leq (h^{\vee})^{-1}H(x,x)H(y,y)$, where $h^{\vee}$ is the dual Coxeter number, with equality exactly for $H$-orthogonal pairs in $τ$-stable long-root subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$. Equivalently, the comass of the Cartan $3$-form with respect to $H$ equals its comass on the compact real form: the spectral norm of the Cartan $3$-form does not increase under complexification. For the Frobenius norm on the image of a representation of Dynkin index $\ell$ the optimal constant is $2/\ell$; this contains the Böttcher--Wenzel and Bloch--Iserles inequalities, extends the latter to complex skew-symmetric matrices, and improves them substantially for the exceptional Lie algebras of types $F_{4}$, $E_{6}$, $E_{7}$, and $E_{8}$. The proof uses the Nahm algebra of $\mathfrak{g}$ with the conjugation induced by $τ$: critical points of the relevant function correspond to $τ$-twisted idempotents, and its Hessian is governed by $τ$-twisted multiplication operators, whose anticommutation with multiplication by $i$ turns the one-sided second order condition at a maximum into a two-sided spectral bound. Subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$ of Dynkin index $j$ give critical points with critical value $1/(jh^{\vee})$, whose Morse indices are computed, and the set of maximum points is a nondegenerate critical manifold. Geometrically, the maximal complex sectional curvature of a compact simple Lie group equals its maximal sectional curvature.

title: BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebras arising from related algebraic structures
author: BakolÈ Louamou, Ibrahima Bakayoko, Kol BÉatrice Gamou
description:
arXiv:2610.11661v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Inspired from some works on constructions of algebraic structures from other ones, we purpose to give some construction theorems on BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebras which unify the notion of the Z2 -graded Poisson algebras, the BiHom-Poisson algebras and their conformal setting. So, we introduce BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebras and show that they are closed under twisting. We then prouve that any regular BiHom-associative conformal algebra leads to BiHom-Poisson conformal algebra via the commutator bracket. Then, we point out that any BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebra together with Rota-Baxter operator give rises to another BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebra. Next, we show that tensor prod- uct of any BiHom-associative superalgebra and any BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebra is also a BiHom-Poisson conformal superalgebra. Contruction from Hom-post-Poisson conformal superalgebras is also given.

title: A Counterexample to Left-Right Symmetry for Diagonal Auslander-Regularity
author: Zhenyu Wang, Zhaoyong Huang, Yu-Zhe Liu
description:
arXiv:2610.11406v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We construct a finite-dimensional Auslander-regular algebra $R$ with global dimension three, which is right diagonal but not left diagonal; moreover, any simple right $R$-module with grade $i$ has projective dimension $i$, but there is a simple left $R$-module with grade one and projective dimension two. It answers a question raised by Iyama negatively.

title: Structure theory of finite solvable Lie conformal algebras
author: Bakhrom Omirov, Yuhui Tan
description:
arXiv:2610.11304v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We develop a structure theory of finite solvable Lie conformal algebras. It is proved that every such algebra admits a Cartan subalgebra, and any two Cartan subalgebras are conjugate by a finite product of exponentials of nilpotent zero modes of elements of the derived algebra. Applied to finite vertex algebras, this yields inner conjugacy of Cartan subalgebras, answering a question of D'Andrea and Marchei. The nilradical and solvable radical of an arbitrary finite Lie conformal algebra are shown to be saturated and invariant under ordinary and conformal derivations. For finite free Lie conformal algebras, we prove a simultaneous diagonalization theorem for conformal tori and characterize the existence of a nonzero torus by explicit identities for constant weights. An example demonstrates that maximal conformal tori of a finite nilpotent Lie conformal algebra can have different ranks, so that conjugacy fails in general. The totally saturated null-filiform Lie conformal algebras admitting a nonzero conformal torus are classified. For each algebra in this classification, we prove that maximal conformal tori have rank one and that the maximal solvable extension with the prescribed nilradical is unique (up to isomorphism) and is the semidirect product with a maximal conformal torus.

title: Affine Schur--Weyl theory for loop Semigroups and polynomial representations
author: Qiang Fu
description:
arXiv:2610.11282v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Classical Schur--Weyl duality plays a fundamental role in the representation theory of general linear and symmetric groups. In this paper, we develop an affine Schur--Weyl theory for the Laurent polynomial loop semigroup. Let $\hat G_K(n)$ denote the Laurent polynomial loop semigroup inside the loop group $GL_n(K((t)))$ over a field $K$, and let $\hat S_K(n,r)$ be the affine Schur algebra. The natural action of $\hat G_K(n)$ on the affine tensor space $Ω_K^{\otimes r}$ induces an algebra homomorphism $K\hat G_K(n)\rightarrow \hat S_K(n,r).$ We prove that this homomorphism is surjective for every field $K$ satisfying $|K|>r$. Furthermore, we establish the double centralizer property for affine Schur algebras over unique factorization domains for all $n\geq2$. For $n\geq2$ and any field $K$ with $|K|>r$, this yields the corresponding centralizer property for $\hat G_K(n)$. In contrast, for $n=1$ and $r\geq2$, the corresponding natural homomorphism is not surjective over any field. For $n\geq 2$, we use the double centralizer theorem to determine the center of the affine Schur algebra and, when $K$ is a field with $|K|>r$, show that $\hatζ_{r,K}$ maps the center of $K\hat G_K(n)$ onto it. Over an algebraically closed field $K$ of arbitrary characteristic, we prove that every finite-dimensional irreducible $\hat S_K(n,r)$-module is a tensor product of evaluation modules. Moreover, we obtain explicit character formulas expressing these irreducible characters as products of characters of irreducible classical Schur algebra modules. Finally, we study polynomial representations of $\hat G_K(n)$ over algebraically closed fields $K$, and classify its finite-dimensional irreducible polynomial representations. For finite fields $\mathbb F_q$ with $q>r$, this yields a classification in the defining-characteristic setting.

title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
author: Alexei Miasnikov, Ivan Shestakov
description:
arXiv:2610.11013v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $δ=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $(x+δt,y+δz,z,t)$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $\ZZ[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted.

title: Lower and Upper Lie Nilpotency Indices of Modular Group Algebras
author: Joe Gildea
description:
arXiv:2610.10915v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We resolve the remaining cases of a longstanding problem on the lower and upper Lie nilpotency indices of modular group algebras. Equality of the two indices has been known in characteristics greater than three since 1992; we establish it in the remaining characteristics two and three, thereby completing the problem for finite groups of prime-power order over finite fields. The proof gives a uniform argument for every prime and introduces a terminal restricted Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt construction that converts the lower-Lie problem into a chronological reachability argument, with no structural hypothesis on the derived subgroup.

title: Strong nonfinite basability of the three-element flat semiring $S_7$
author: Mengya Yue, Xiaolei Shao
description:
arXiv:2610.14068v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We prove that the three-element flat semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based within the class of additively idempotent semirings. More generally, let $\mathcal N$ be the subvariety of $\Var(S_7)$ defined by $x^2y\approx x^2$. For every finite ai-semiring $A$, each variety $\mathcal W$ satisfying $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal W\subseteq\Var(A)$ has infinite axiomatic rank.

title: $W$-algebras with involution: polynomial identities and asymptotic growth
author: Ginevra Giordani, Antonio Ioppolo, Carla Rizzo
description:
arXiv:2610.10406v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $W$ be an algebra with involution over a field of characteristic zero. We develop a theory of $W$-polynomial identities with involution for finite-dimensional $(W,*)$-algebras $A$, using the multiplier algebra with involution of $A$. We prove that the $(W,*)$-exponent of $A$ exists and coincides with the ordinary $*$-exponent. We then consider a four-dimensional subalgebra $M$ of the algebra of $4\times4$ upper triangular matrices, endowed with the reflection involution, and study two non-equivalent $(W,*)$-algebra structures on it. For both structures, we determine the corresponding $T_W^*$-ideals of $W$-polynomial identities with involution and compute the $(W,*)$-codimension sequences explicitly; for one of them, we also determine the complete $(W,*)$-cocharacter sequence. Finally, we prove that these two $W$-algebras with involution generate distinct varieties of almost polynomial growth.

title: Higher Fomin-Kirillov algebras are infinite-dimensional
author: N. Andruskiewitsch, I. Angiono, I. Heckenberger, S. Lentner, C. Reiher, L. Vendramin
description:
arXiv:2610.10144v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We show that the Fomin--Kirillov algebras $FK_n$ are infinite-dimensional for $n\geq6$. This answers a question posed by Fomin and Kirillov in 1997. To prove this, we demonstrate that the Nichols algebras supported on the conjugacy class of transpositions of the symmetric group are infinite-dimensional for both relevant 2-cocycles. For this, we develop a new method of partially semisimplifying a Nichols algebra along an automorphism of order $p$ in characteristic $p$.

title: From bosonized $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to liftings of the super Jordan plane
author: Tao Lu
description:
arXiv:2610.10098v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study a family of liftings $\mathfrak U(λ)$ of the super Jordan plane over the infinite cyclic group in characteristic zero. For a nonzero lifting parameter $λ$, we identify a natural subalgebra $\mathfrak B$ with the bosonization of $U(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$, also known as $sl_{-1}(2)$, and show that the lifting $\mathfrak U(λ)$ is obtained from $\mathfrak B$ by an Ore localization at a single distinguished element. This structural description provides a unified approach to the representation theory and ideal structure of $\mathfrak U(λ)$. We classify the finite-dimensional simple modules of $\mathfrak B$ and prove that every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak B$-module is completely reducible; the localization then yields the corresponding results for $\mathfrak U(λ)$. We determine the prime, primitive, and completely prime ideals of both algebras. Finally, we compute their classical quotient rings, showing in particular that the classical quotient ring of $\mathfrak U(λ)$ is a $2\times2$ matrix algebra over the skew field of fractions of the tensor product of its centre and the first Weyl algebra.

title: Ramified Quivers with Potentials, Monodromy Characters, and Cluster Bases I
author: Jiarui Fei
description:
arXiv:2610.09868v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We construct categorical models and cluster characters for skew-symmetrizable cluster algebras admitting good ramified realizations. Goodness is equivalent to nondegenerate realizability. When a reddening sequence is given, it is enough to check sign coherence of the arrow types along that sequence. Triangular extensions with arbitrary connecting bimodule types preserve goodness when both component matrices admit reddening sequences. Consequently, every matrix obtained from one vertex by triangular extensions and mutations admits a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization for every compatible positive integral symmetrizer. For a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization, the monodromy $F$-polynomials satisfy mutation for all finite decorated representations, without a rigidity hypothesis. A full initial order determines valued universal presentations and their cluster characters. Under the reachability condition, these characters form a basis of the middle cluster algebra for arbitrary geometric coefficients, with frozen variables inverted, and contain all cluster monomials. title: The algebraic classification of five-dimensional nilpotent right alternative algebras
author: Zohida Raxmatova, Aloberdi Sattarov
description:
arXiv:2610.09816v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We develop the method of central extensions (the Skjelbred--Sund method) for nilpotent right alternative algebras over the field of complex numbers and apply it to obtain the algebraic classification of five-dimensional nilpotent right alternative algebras. More precisely, we classify, up to isomorphism, all complex five-dimensional nilpotent right alternative algebras that have no annihilator component (that is, which are not a direct sum of a smaller algebra and a one-dimensional algebra with zero product) and which are not $2$-step nilpotent. Every such algebra is a non-split central extension of a nontrivial nilpotent right alternative algebra of dimension three (by a two-dimensional space) or of dimension four (by a one-dimensional space). For each of the relevant three- and four-dimensional algebras we compute the second cohomology space, the automorphism group and its action on the second cohomology, and we determine all orbits that give non-split extensions. The resulting list consists of $124$ algebras and families of algebras; it contains $29$ algebras with two-dimensional annihilator and $95$ algebras with one-dimensional annihilator.

title: Symmetry and Invariant Theory of Quadratic Dynamics over Eight-Dimensional Composition Algebras
author: Daniele Corradetti
description:
arXiv:2610.09544v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: The iteration of $z\mapsto z^2+c$ over the octonions has been drawn for more than thirty years, and it is known that the octonionic Julia sets are bodies of revolution about the imaginary part of the constant. Real eight-dimensional composition algebras, however, are much richer than the octonions: beside the Hurwitz algebras there are the symmetric composition algebras, the para-octonions and the Okubo algebras, which have no unit and whose automorphism groups are $G_2$ and $PSU(3)$ respectively. In this work we study, to our knowledge for the first time, the quadratic dynamics over these algebras, and we do it in an experimental spirit: an atlas of 134 four-dimensional renderings, measured quarter by quarter, suggests the statements, which we then prove and test against new, predicted pictures. We show that the symmetries of the Julia sets of the Okubo algebra are governed by the root decomposition of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ with respect to the plane of $1$ and $i$: for a constant in that plane the continuous symmetry is a maximal torus, which acts by rotations on three root planes and grows to $U(2)$ on the Weyl walls; the automorphism group of the symmetrized product is $PSU(3)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$. We then prove that the Mandelbrot set with seed $0$ of every symmetric composition algebra is the pull-back of a single planar set through the invariants $n(c)$ and $n(c,c\diamond c)$: the tricorn in the compact case, the tricorn and a hyperbolic tricorn in the split case. The result is quite surprising since the para-octonionic and the Okubonic Mandelbrot sets turn out to be the same planar figure saturated by two different groups. Finally, we show that every bilateral map over a symmetric composition algebra is an octonionic quadratic map in disguise, and that at the Petersson angle $θ=90^\circ$ the dynamics acquires symmetries that do not come from automorphisms.

title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
author: Andrey Yurkov
description:
arXiv:2610.14060v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices. To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.

title: Effective computation of Moore-Penrose inverses over fields of rational functions by specializations
author: Juana Sendra
description:
arXiv:2610.08676v2 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: In this paper we consider matrices whose entries are rational functions of several parameters over a Moore-Penrose field, that is, a field with an involutory automorphism over which every matrix has Moore-Penrose inverse. We prove that over any such field the Penrose conditions can be solved with linear algebra alone, even though they form a polynomial system of degree two. We then bound the degrees of the numerator and of the denominator of the pseudoinverse in terms of the degree of the entries and of the rank, and not of the dimensions of the matrix. Specialization is the thread: the closed form is computed once over the field of rational functions, and the question is at which parameter values it still returns the pseudoinverse of the specialized matrix. We determine the values where it does not, from the matrix alone and before computing the pseudoinverse. They are the zeros of a polynomial built from the maximal minors, and they are the values at which the rank decreases. This turns previous sufficient conditions into an exact characterization. The theory also gives symbolic algorithms for the real, the complex and the parametric case, which we implement in Maple and test on 972 timed replications. We also apply them to a Leontief economic model, where the excluded value is the point at which the economy stops being viable.

title: New integer sequence OEIS A392714 counts Wronskians: fast evaluation via late-growing permutations
author: Kian C. Shah, Arthemy V. Kiselev
description:
arXiv:2610.08636v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: The alternating composition of $N = 2p$ weighted differential operators $w_j(x)\cdot\partial_x^{\,p}$ of strict order $p$ on the line $\mathbb{R} \ni x$ is again an operator of order $p$; its coefficient is the universal constant $c(p)$ times the Wronskian of the weights $w_1,\ldots,w_N$. Lie brackets of vector fields fix $c(p=1)=1$; we want to find $c(p \geqslant 2)$: e.g., $c(2) = 2$ or $c(3) = 90$. Direct symbolic expansion (over $|S_{2p}| =(2p)!$ permutations) fails for $p \geqslant 4$. Taking the monomials $w_j = x^{j-1}$ reduces the summation to the much smaller set $Φ_p \subseteq S_{2p-1} \subsetneq S_{2p}$ of late-growing permutations. Expressing $c(p)$ as a signed sum of products of falling factorials, we implement and speed up the algorithm that gains all the integer values up to $c(18) = 4.881\ldots \cdot 10^{462}$. The resulting sequence is new, now registered as OEIS A392714; its (sub)leading-order growth rate is $\log c(p) \simeq 2p^2\log p -b p^2 + \overline{o}(p^2)$ for $p\gg 1$, with $b\geqslant 2.6744$.

title: Group-ring methods for Alexander quandle rings
author: Zhi-Lin Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.08204v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For an Alexander quandle on an abelian group $G$ with automorphism $φ$, we identify its augmentation powers and nonunital commutator subalgebra with explicit ideals in the ordinary group ring over any commutative unital coefficient ring. Each left-normed augmentation power is also the span of all products with the same number of factors, independently of parenthesization. Over $\mathbb{Z}$, we determine every successive augmentation quotient for Alexander quandles on nontrivial finite cyclic groups. For an even dihedral quandle of order $m \ge 4$, every quotient in degree $r \ge 2$ is $(\mathbb{Z}/(m/2)\mathbb{Z})^2$; this proves the proposed replacement for the disproved order-$m$ prediction. For the integral quandle ring of $\operatorname{Core}(\mathbb{Z})$, we describe all augmentation powers, determine the nonunital commutator subalgebra, and prove that the difference of the basis elements indexed by 1 and 0 does not lie in the square of the augmentation ideal. When $(1-φ)G$ is a finite $p$-group, the integral filtration is separated, so every nonzero integral idempotent has augmentation one. Fourier analysis shows that finite odd-order commutative Alexander quandles have only zero and the basis elements as integral idempotents. Combined with the midpoint description of medial commutative quandles, this gives the same classification for every finite medial commutative quandle. Finally, the complex quandle algebra of the core of any nontrivial finite abelian group of odd order has right Peirce spectrum $\{0,1,-1\}$, proving the conjectured odd-order dihedral spectrum.

title: Extensions of Restricted Simple Modules for Restricted Lie Algebras of Cartan Type
author: Chao Ma
description:
arXiv:2610.08184v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We determine the first extension groups between simple restricted modules for the restricted simple Lie algebras of Cartan type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, which answers the restricted case of a problem of Benkart and Feldvoss. Extensions from parabolically induced modules are computed by finite restricted-cohomology complexes of the grading parabolic, and for the exceptional modules we obtain closed formulas in all four families. Neither the trivial module nor any nontrivial exceptional simple has self-extensions. In characteristic seven we determine the quiver of $S(3;1)^{(1)}$, which has 49 vertices and 566 arrows.

title: Diagonalizable modular derivations on bigraded Poisson spaces and Koszul duality
author: Ruobing Chen, Di Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.08091v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For two bigraded spaces $k^{m||n}$ and $k^{n\wedge m}$ equipped with appropriate quadratic Poisson structures, Koszul duality identifies the mixed Poisson differential calculi and, in the unimodular case, their Poisson cohomologies as Batalin--Vilkovisky algebras. In the current paper we prove that Koszul duality induces an isomorphism of Batalin--Vilkovisky algebras between their Poisson cohomologies when the modular derivation of one algebra is diagonalizable, including non-unimodular cases.

title: Molnár's Theorem for split $C^*$-by-nilpotent algebras
author: Mario Galici, Gianmarco La Rosa, Manuel Mancini, Gábor P. Nagy
description:
arXiv:2610.08010v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Kubo-Ando means are a rich class of important binary operations on the set of positive elements of an operator algebra. The aim of this article is to understand the algebraic structure of these operations. We generalize a recent result of L. Molnár for $C^*$-algebras to the class of split $C^*$-by-nilpotent algebras by using the method of analytic local expansion of binary operations. Eventually, we prove that in any $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$, the identity $[x,[y,z]]=0$ implies commutativity.

title: Nilpotent Product Probability of Finite Rings
author: Dibyasman Sarma, Tikaram Subedi
description:
arXiv:2610.07892v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For a finite ring $R$, we investigate the probability that the product of two randomly chosen elements in $R$ is nilpotent, which we call the nilpotent product probability (NPP) of $R$ and denote by $P_{nil}(R)$. We derive bounds for $P_{nil}(R)$ that depend on the structure of $R$, and prove that among all commutative rings with identity, the class of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ attains the maximum value of NPP, which is equal to $3/4$. Further, we determine the set of all values of NPP for commutative rings with identity and classify all rings attaining those values. Finally, we investigate the relationship between NPP of $R$ and NPP of some subrings of the matrix ring over $R$.

title: Hereditary NC Polynomials & Positivity Domains
author: Abdellah Islam, Jurij Volčič, Hugo J. Woerdeman
description:
arXiv:2610.14053v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Noncommutative polynomials, elements of the free algebra generated by several noncommuting variables $x_1,...,x_g,x_1^*,...,x_g^*$, are of importance in noncommutative algebra, free analysis and real algebraic geometry. We allow matrix coefficients and view these noncommutative polynomials as functions in several size-free matrix variables. The free locus of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ is the sequence of hypersurfaces $\mathscr{Z}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:\det f(X) = 0\}$. When $f$ is Hermitian, the positivity domain of $f$ is the sequence of semialgebraic sets $\mathcal{D}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:f(X)\text{ is positive semidefinite}\}$. We show for well-behaved cases that the Euclidean boundary of the positivity domain is Zariski dense in the free locus. This leads to a certificate for equality of positivity domains of coefficient-irreducible unsignatured atomic quadratics. Finally, we describe the geometric structure of positivity domains of hereditary quadratic polynomials through $Γ$-convexity.

title: Symmetric Grassmann Formulas: Monotone Dimension-Defect Hierarchies
author: Masoud Gharahi, Diego Ponterio
description:
arXiv:2610.06739v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study the dimension defect of finitely many subspaces over an arbitrary field. We derive a symmetric, nonrecursive Grassmann-type formula for the dimension of their sum. The formula expresses the total dimension loss through intersections of a distinguished subspace with partial sums of the remaining subspaces, with coefficients determined by the number of subspaces involved. We also show that the formula admits a Shapley-value interpretation for the associated representable polymatroid. Grouping the correction terms by the number of participating subspaces yields a nonnegative dimension-defect profile. We prove that this profile is monotone and identify its successive gaps with the discrete curvatures of the average-rank profile. These gaps give exact remainders in two-sided defect bounds. Equality in either bound holds precisely when the images of the subspaces in the quotient by their common intersection form an internal direct sum. We also give an exact geometric decomposition of the Kinser slack into nonnegative quotient dimensions and characterize equality. Averaging these slacks over permutations and contractions recovers every defect curvature except the final one; additional representability constraints remain in the individual ordered slacks. Weighted and dual formulas accompany the expansion, and entropy analogues express the defect levels and curvatures as averages of mutual and conditional mutual information, respectively.

title: Graded bimodules over split group algebras: stabilizers and Peirce decompositions
author: Felipe de Mattos Chafik Hindi, Waldeck Schutzer
description:
arXiv:2610.06072v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We classify, up to graded isomorphism, graded bimodules over split group algebras of finite abelian subgroups of an arbitrary group. The classification is governed by double cosets, stabilizer characters, and coefficient modules. Over a field, we determine the essential image of the induction functor on Yetter-Drinfel'd modules, giving a negative answer to a question of Dos Santos and Yasumura in the nonabelian case. We also compute the Peirce components and characterize multiplicity-free bimodules through extensions of stabilizer characters.

author: Morteza Ahmadi
description:
arXiv:2610.05862v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We extend the theory of Baer, Rickart, and their local, graded, and $*$-analogues for Steinberg algebras. First, we prove that positive definiteness passes from the coefficient field to the Steinberg algebra, and that this, together with graded von Neumann regularity, characterized by Steinberg and van Wyk, yields graded locally Rickart $*$-Steinberg algebras. Then we show that local Baer behavior forces every compact open subset of the unit space to be extremally disconnected. Consequently, when compact open subspaces of the unit space are metrizable, local Baer behavior forces the groupoid to be discrete. In the discrete case, we use the orbit-by-orbit decomposition into finitary matrix algebras over isotropy group algebras to convert annihilator conditions into explicit matrix conditions. For groupoids whose isotropy is trivial or infinite cyclic, these ingredients yield complete local and unital characterizations. In particular, local Baer and graded local Baer conditions are equivalent to discreteness, while the ungraded local Baer $*$-condition additionally requires that every orbit with nontrivial isotropy be a singleton. We then apply the theory to boundary path groupoids. Using the Steinberg algebra model, we obtain the Rickart, Baer, and Baer $*$ characterizations of Leavitt path algebras, including the local and graded variants.

title: Genus of quaternion algebras over formally real fields
author: Sergey V. Tikhonov
description:
arXiv:2610.05392v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We prove the finiteness of the genus of quaternion division algebras over some formally real fields. In particular, if $F$ is a formally real field and the second power of the fundamental ideal $I^2(F)$ is torsion-free, then the genus of any quaternion division $F$-algebra is trivial. For instance, this immediately implies that the genus vanishes for any quaternion division algebra over a formally real pythagorean field. The proofs are based on methods from the theory of quadratic forms.

title: Hypergraphs associated to skew polynomial algebras and surface triangulations
author: Akihiro Higashitani, Kenta Ueyama
description:
arXiv:2610.05311v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study the realization problem for point schemes of skew polynomial algebras. We approach this problem combinatorially by translating it into the study of certain $3$-uniform hypergraphs, which we call point hypergraphs. We first give a homological criterion characterizing point hypergraphs. Using this criterion, we study hypergraphs obtained by deleting triangles from triangulations of connected orientable closed surfaces. Deleting exactly one triangle always gives a non-point hypergraph. When the triangulation has no separating nonfacial $3$-cycles, deleting either no triangles or at least two triangles gives a point hypergraph, and the one-triangle deletions are minimal non-point hypergraphs with respect to taking induced sub-hypergraphs. It follows that point hypergraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced sub-hypergraphs. Next, for each point hypergraph, we construct an affine moduli variety of skew polynomial algebras realizing it, and determine its dimension. For point hypergraphs arising from the above surface construction, we obtain an explicit dimension formula in terms of the number of vertices, the Euler characteristic, and the number of deleted triangles. Finally, we characterize point hypergraphs on six vertices in terms of a four-vertex local condition together with a single exceptional obstruction.

title: Sparse Moore-local realisations of binary irreducible polynomials on near-square lattice regions
author: Lizhong Chen
description:
arXiv:2610.06983v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For every $N\ge36$, we realise any prescribed monic irreducible binary polynomial of degree $N$ as the characteristic polynomial of a linear hybrid cellular automaton on a near-square region of exactly $N$ cells. The transition matrix is Moore-local with a null boundary and has at most $3N-1$ directed nonself dependencies. The dependency graph retains a bidirectional Hamilton path; its indegree, outdegree and underlying undirected degree are at most six. The underlying graph contains an explicit square grid minor of side proportional to $\sqrt N$. The deterministic synthesis takes $O(N^3)$ bit operations. The construction combines a local similarity transformation with a transport potential and joint routing across consecutive row gaps. Exact verification of finite certificates, followed by induction, proves the required routing inequalities for every admissible width. We also give an entirely analytic construction with fewer than $7N/2$ dependencies and prove a lower bound of $5N/2-O(\sqrt N)$ for the retained path and full rectangular grid minor. This lower bound is sharp when the characteristic polynomial is unrestricted.

title: $n$-Valued Analogue of Abel's Theorem
author: Mikhail Kornev
description:
arXiv:2610.14044v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Abel's classical theorem shows that a continuously differentiable one-dimensional associative law with a two-sided unit is locally equivalent to addition under a change of coordinate. We prove an $n$-valued analogue in the algebraic and formal settings. Over a field of characteristic zero, every associative algebraic $n$-valued monoid on $\mathbb P^1$ with a strong two-sided unit is commutative. Over a reduced commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra, any one-dimensional formal $n$-valued group is commutative. We then classify $n$-valued formal groups over arbitrary $\mathbb Q$-algebras that are integral domains: for any $n$-valued formal group there is a unique divisor $m$ of $n$ such that the law is strongly isomorphic to the $n/m$-fold diagonal of the cyclic elementary $m$-valued law $\mathbb G_m$. This proves Kholodov's classification conjecture over integral domain $\mathbb Q$-algebras.

title: Formal Matrix Rings with the Involution Property
author: Valeriya Kirova
description:
arXiv:2610.04709v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study formal matrix rings with the involution property, that is, rings in which every element can be represented as the sum of an invertible element and an involution. After recalling the construction of formal matrix rings via Morita contexts, we describe involutions in triangular formal matrix rings and establish a criterion for upper triangular rings of order two. We then prove that a formal matrix ring of arbitrary finite order has the involution property whenever all of its diagonal rings have this property. Several examples and counterexamples are included to illustrate the obtained results.

title: Cartan inverse semigroups and twisted Steinberg algebras
author: Nathan Brownlowe, Lisa Orloff Clark, Ying-Fen Lin, Lynnel D. Naingue
description:
arXiv:2610.04548v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We introduce the notion of a Cartan inverse semigroup and an (algebraic) semi-Cartan subalgebra in an $R$-algebra A, providing a purely algebraic analogue of Cartan semigroups and semi-Cartan subalgebras in a C*-algebra. This extends the theory of quasi-Cartan subalgebras, shifting the focus from designated subalgebras to designated subsemigroups. Our main result characterises twisted Steinberg algebras in terms of the existence of a Cartan inverse semigroup: we show that an $R$-algebra admits a Cartan inverse semigroup if and only if it is isomorphic to a twisted Steinberg algebra. Moreover, when our construction is applied to a twisted Steinberg algebra over an ample Hausdorff groupoid, the constructed twist is naturally isomorphic to the original one.

title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
author: Thiago Castilho De Mello, Prachi Saini
description:
arXiv:2610.04466v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $Φ(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $Φ$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $Φ$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.

title: Characterization of the centrally finite Amitsur-Small division rings
author: Elad Paran
description:
arXiv:2610.04317v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: In 1978, Amitsur and Small asked whether, for every division ring $D$, maximal left ideals of $D[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ contract to maximal left ideals in smaller polynomial subrings. Chapman and the author showed that the answer is negative in general and called $D$ an Amitsur-Small ring when this contraction property always holds. Earlier work showed that Hamilton's real quaternion algebra is Amitsur-Small, that division algebras of degree three are not Amitsur-Small, and that degree-two examples are restricted to a specific quaternionic form; subsequent work excluded cyclic division algebras of odd prime degree. We give a complete resolution in the centrally finite case. If $D$ has finite dimension over its center $F$, then $D$ is an Amitsur-Small ring if and only if either $D=F$, or $F$ is real closed and $D$ is the Hamilton quaternion algebra $(-1,-1)_F$. In every other noncommutative centrally finite case, failure already occurs in two variables: there is a maximal left ideal $M\subseteq D[x,y]$ such that $M\cap D[x]$ is not maximal in $D[x]$.

title: Finite-dimensional Lie subalgebras of the universal enveloping algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$
author: Tim Heib
description:
arXiv:2610.04001v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: In this work we provide the complete classification of all non-zero finite-dimensional complex Lie subalgebras of the universal enveloping algebra of the special linear Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$. That is, we show that every such nilpotent Lie subalgebra is abelian and every non-solvable Lie subalgebra is reductive, with semisimple component isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$ itself. Every non-nilpotent solvable Lie subalgebra is the direct sum of an abelian center and a member of the family of solvable Lie algebras $\mathfrak{r}(\boldsymbol{d},\boldsymbol{m})$, parameterized by a vector $\boldsymbol{d}$ whose entries are strictly increasing positive integers that have greatest common divisor one together with a positive integer vector $\boldsymbol{m}$ of the same length recording their multiplicities. Moreover, we discuss the corresponding classification in a real skew-hermitian setting and its relation to the realizations in the single- and two-mode Weyl algebras.

title: Generalizing the $A^A$ Problem for Finite Ordered Sets
author: George Grätzer
description:
arXiv:2610.03986v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let X and Y be finite ordered sets and let $X^Y$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $Y$ to $X$. Let $t$ be a~term formed from a~single variable by exponentiation. We prove that, for every term $t$ with at most twelve variable occurrences and arbitrary finite ordered sets $A,B$, $t(A)\cong t(B)$ implies that $A\cong B$. General constructions and reconstruction principles are developed first; the second part gives the occurrence-by-occurrence proofs. At twelve occurrences the proof covers 4,766 interchange normal forms, representing all 58,786 binary parenthesizations, including 40 exceptional forms. Two additional unbounded reconstruction families, complete finite audit data, and 457 exact height-comparison certificates are included.

title: Signed seeds and G-gradings on cluster algebras
author: Lauren Williams, Alan Yan
description:
arXiv:2610.03612v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: The theory of cluster algebras is closely connected to the theory of total positivity; indeed, the desire to better understand total positivity was one of the main motivations for Fomin and Zelevinsky's introduction of cluster algebras [arXiv:math/0104151]. In particular, any cluster variety whose coordinate ring has a cluster structure has a natural notion of positive part: the subset of the variety where all cluster variables are positive. In this paper, we explain that there are other signed cells contained in cluster varieties that are equally natural from a cluster-theoretic point of view. These come from signed seeds, which can be thought of as a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-grading on cluster variables, and which were introduced in [arXiv:2310.17727] in the context of the amplituhedron. More generally, given any abelian group $G$, we introduce the notion of a $G$-graded seed for a cluster algebra, which is a way of assigning elements of $G$ to each cluster variable which is compatible with the cluster structure. When $G$ is the multiplicative group $\{-1, 1\}$, this recovers the above notion of signed seed; when $G = \mathbb{C}^*$, this recovers the notion of cluster automorphism group [GSV10] or cluster dilation group [arXiv:2603.17890]; and when $G = \mathbb{Z}^d$, this recovers the notion of graded cluster algebra studied by Grabowski-Launois [arXiv:1301.2133], Grabowski [arXiv:1309.6170] and Gekhtman-Shapiro-Vainshtein [GSV10, Section 5.2] (which had previously appeared in special cases in work of Fomin-Zelevinsky [arXiv:math/0602259]). The examples we study include the space of square matrices, symmetric matrices, skew-symmetric matrices, positroid varieties, and amplituhedron tiles. We also connect this notion to tropical mutation when $G = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$.

title: (Super)nilpotency and solvability in algebras with zero
author: Ivana Đurđev, Nebojša Mudrinski
description:
arXiv:2610.03348v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: An algebra with zero is an algebra that contains an element 0, called zero, such that all fundamental operations have the property that the result is zero whenever at least one of the arguments takes the value 0. We introduce the notion of the higher commutator of ideals and Rees congruences for such algebras. It is shown that the commutator of Rees congruences is equal to the Rees congruence of the commutator of the corresponding ideals. We apply this result to provide characterisations of n-supernilpotency and n-nilpotency in algebras with zero, as well as n-solvability in groupoids with zero.

author: Nurken Smadyarov
description:

Abstract: An algebra is called binary Zinbiel if every subalgebra generated by at most two elements is a Zinbiel algebra. Over a field of characteristic zero, we prove that every finite-dimensional binary Zinbiel algebra is nilpotent. We also show that a subvariety of binary Zinbiel algebras is nil if and only if it does not contain the variety of all Zinbiel algebras. We further prove an analogue of Itô's theorem for binary Zinbiel algebras.

author: Ahmed M. Adly
description:

Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero and $D_N(a_n)=a_{n+1}a_{n+2}$ the adjacent-quadratic locally nilpotent derivation on $A_N=k[a_0,\dots,a_N]$. We determine the invariant ring at $N=5$, where deleting $a_0$ gives the polynomial base kernel $B^{D_5}=K=k[p,q,J_1,J_2]$, so localization gives the polynomial-line invariant algebra $(A_5^{D_5})_{pq}=K_{pq}[W]$ with $W=F_0/(p^2q^4)$, but this does not by itself determine the global kernel. An invariant $H$ of weight $24$ and $a_0$-degree $2$ lies outside $K[F_0]$, and adjoining it gives the six-generator hypersurface $C_5$; the obstruction is explained by algebraic residue behavior defeating naive denominator descent. An invariant $F_{46}^{int}$ of weight $46$ and $a_0$-degree $4$ lies outside $C_5$ and satisfies $p^2F_{46}^{int}\in C_5$. To pass from this candidate to the full invariant ring, a second slice chart arising from $f_{13}$, together with exact $q$- and $p$-saturation, yields $A_5^{D_5}=C_5[F_{46}^{int}]$, hence finite generation, with a codimension-two complete-intersection presentation and explicit Hilbert series. title: Prime-Power Multiplicative Modular Monoid Morphisms
author: Joseph Atalaye, Liam Baker, Sophie Marques
description:
arXiv:2610.02393v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We undertake a systematic study of multiplicative monoid morphisms between prime-power modular monoids $(\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z},\cdot)$ and $(\mathbb{Z}/q^f\mathbb{Z},\cdot)$, for arbitrary primes $p,q$ and integers $e,f\geq 1$. Our approach proceeds in three stages. We first determine the hom-set $\mathbf{Hom}(U_{p^e},U_{q^f})$ of group morphisms between the corresponding unit groups and exhibit explicit isomorphisms describing its group structure. We then identify the subset $\mathcal{H}_{p^e,q^f,v}$ of unit group morphisms that extend to full monoid morphisms on $(\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z},\cdot)$, characterizing it via explicit divisibility conditions and describing its algebraic structure. Finally, we give a complete description of $\mathbf{Hom}_{\mathbf{Mon}}((\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z},\cdot), (\mathbb{Z}/q^f\mathbb{Z},\cdot))$ and establish an explicit monoid isomorphism between this hom-set and a naturally defined monoid built from unit groups of lower-level modular rings.

title: On The Index of Polynomial Compositions over Valued Fields
author: Anuj Jakhar, Ravi Kalwaniya, Shanta Laishram, Prabhakar Yadav
description:
arXiv:2610.02111v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Determining whether an algebraic number field admits a power integral basis is a classical problem, but it can be difficult for fields defined by polynomial compositions and dynamical iterates. In this paper, we study the monogeneity of compositions $f(h(x))$, where $f(x)$ and $h(x)$ are monic polynomials over an arbitrary Krull valuation ring and $h(x)$ is a trinomial. We derive explicit formulas for the discriminant of the composition and use them to characterize when $f(h(x))$ generates a monogenic field. In particular, we relate the monogeneity of the composition to that of $f(x)$ and to explicit square-free conditions on the critical values of $h(x)$. We further extend the results to polynomial iteration and obtain a criterion for the monogeneity of binomial iterates, yielding new infinite families of monogenic fields. Finally, we give quantitative results and illustrate our criteria with several examples.

title: Dimension subrings of Lie rings
author: Vasily Ionin, Roman Mikhailov, Tima Petrov
description:
arXiv:2610.02042v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We show that, unlike the lower central series, the dimension series of a Lie ring need not stabilize when two consecutive terms coincide; in fact, arbitrarily long finite plateaux occur. We prove that $D_n(L)/γ_{n+1}(L)$ is central in $L/γ_{n+1}(L)$ for every $n\geq1$, in contrast to the group case. If $c\geq2$ and $L$ is metabelian and nilpotent of class at most $c$, we prove that $D_{2c-1}(L)=0$. In particular, our results imply that $D_5(L)\subseteqγ_4(L)$ for every Lie ring $L$.

title: Invertibility of structured perturbations of singular matrices over unital rings
author: Johan Öinert
description:
arXiv:2610.01948v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: In this article, we study the invertibility of matrices of the form $A+EDF$, where $A$ and $D$ are square matrices over a unital, not necessarily commutative, ring and $A$ is singular. Under natural hypotheses on kernels and images, we prove that $A+EDF$ is invertible if and only if $D$ is invertible, and obtain an explicit formula for the inverse of $A+EDF$ by purely algebraic methods. When the coefficient ring is stably finite, or more specifically a field, we obtain an invertibility criterion under weaker hypotheses. Our results extend and sharpen a theorem of Eriksson and Nordqvist for complex matrices.

title: Ideals of homomorphic images of the enveloping algebra of the Witt algebra
author: Tuan Anh Pham
description:
arXiv:2610.01913v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Let $W_{\geq -1} = \mathbb{C}[t]\partial$ and $W = \mathbb{C}[t, t^{-1}]\partial$ be the Witt algebra of algebraic vector fields on $\mathbb{C}$ and $\mathbb{C}^*$ respectively. In this paper, we make significant progress toward the open conjecture that the enveloping algebras $\mathrm{U}(W_{\geq -1})$ and $\mathrm{U}(W)$ satisfy the ascending chain condition (ACC) on two-sided ideals. We show that all homomorphic images of $\mathrm{U}(W_{\geq -1})$ and $\mathrm{U}(W)$ under the family of ``orbit homomorphisms'' of arbitrary Gelfand-Kirillov dimension satisfy ACC on ideals. These orbit homomorphisms were the key ingredient allowing us to ``lift'' the Dixmier map from finite-dimensional solvable settings to infinite-dimensional settings of the Witt and Virasoro algebras in our recent work [Pham, 2025, arXiv:2504.14670]. As a result, we completely classify the prime and primitive spectra of these homomorphic images. As these images approximate $\mathrm{U}(W_{\geq -1})$ better as their GK-dimension increases, this classification sheds new light on the two-sided and prime ideal structures of $\mathrm{U}(W_{\geq -1})$. Finally, we discuss several applications of our results to the Dixmier map for $W_{\geq -1}$.

title: The Derived Algebra of Nonlinear Polynomial Divergence-Free Vector Fields
author: Chao Ma
description:
arXiv:2610.01838v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We study the Lie algebra $L_{\ge2}$ of divergence-free polynomial vector fields on $k^n$, $n\ge3$, with coefficients of degree at least two, graded by coefficient degree. Over every field its derived algebra in degree $d\ge3$ is the space of exact fields, those whose contraction with the volume form is an exact form, and it is already spanned by brackets with quadratic fields. In characteristic zero this is the whole degree-$d$ component. In characteristic $p>0$ the abelianization is nonzero above degree two exactly in the degrees $d\ge(p-1)(n-1)$ with $d\equiv1-n\pmod p$, and Cartier descent identifies it with a Frobenius twist of a rational $\mathrm{GL}_n$-module, tensored with a power of the determinant. For $p\ge5$ each exact component is obtained from the previous one by bracketing with quadratic fields.

title: On a Rank Nullstellensatz Conjecture for Noncommutative Polynomials
author: Sizhuo Yan, Jianting Yang
description:
arXiv:2610.01804v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: Jurij Volčič conjectured that a noncommutative polynomial $g$ belongs to the two-sided ideal generated by $f_1,\ldots,f_l$ if and only if, for matrices of every size, the rank of the evaluation of $g$ is bounded by a constant times the maximum rank of the evaluations of $f_1,\ldots,f_l$. In this paper, we show this equivalence when the generators $f_1,\ldots,f_l$ are homogeneous. We then give an explicit counterexample in the non-homogeneous case.

title: The Weight Criterion, Dong Property, and Manin Products of Operads
author: P. Kolesnikov, B. Sartayev
description:
arXiv:2610.01798v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: We establish that, for a binary operad Var, the Hadamard product of Var and the operad Nov of Novikov algebras is a binary operad (i.e., coincides with their Manin white product Nov $\circ$ Var) if and only if the quadratic part of Var governs a 2-variety. The condition Nov $\circ$ Var $=$ Nov $\otimes$ Var is known to be equivalent to the existence of an easily verifiable characterization of those differential Var-polynomials which lie in the free derived Var-algebra. For a binary quadratic operad, these conditions are also equivalent to the Dong property of formal distributions. We distinguish the white product defined as a generated sub-operad from its quadratic approximation and give an example in which the canonical epimorphism between them is not injective.

title: The Comon Rank Gap of a Third-Order Symmetric Tensor Can Exceed One
author: Jianze Li
description:
arXiv:2610.01660v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: For a third-order symmetric tensor, the Comon rank gap is the difference between its CP rank and its symmetric rank. We study direct sums of Lovitz's rational $27$-dimensional tensor, whose two ranks are $55$ and $56$. Two copies have ranks $110$ and $112$, and three copies have ranks $165$ and $168$, over both the real and the complex fields. Thus direct sums yield concise cubic tensors on spaces of dimensions $54$ and $81$ with Comon rank gaps two and three.

title: Local and 2 local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivation of $n$-dimensional totally graded filiform Lie algebras
author: Farkhodzhon Arzikulov, Mirzobek Shodiev
description:
arXiv:2610.01556v1 Announce Type: historical recovery 
Abstract: This article provides a complete algebraic description of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations, local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations, and 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations on $n$-dimensional totally graded complex filiform Lie algebras of maximum length. Based on the foundational classification framework established by Janez Bernik (2020), we systematically determine the vector spaces of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations for the six infinite structural sequences ($m_0(n)$, $m_2(n)$, $W^+(n)$, $m_{0,1}(n)$, $m_{0,2}(n)$, $m_{0,3}(n)$) and the five exceptional one-parameter families ($g_{7,α}$ through $g_{11,α}$). By analyzing the pointwise local evaluation equations via parametric matrix systems, we establish the structural linearity and rigidity of local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. In contrast, we demonstrate that the independent parameters residing in the boundary rows of the $\frac{1}{2}$-derivation matrices provide sufficient degrees of freedom to bypass linearity constraints. Exploiting these boundary configurations, we explicitly construct pure non-linear and non-additive 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations leveraging the homogeneous function of degree one, $f(z_1, z_2) = z_1^3 / (z_1^2 + z_2^2)$, thereby defining the exact boundary where local rigidity fails.
